title: The grapes
subtitle: Whites and mountain reds
objectives: Name the region's main white grapes

steps.title: Whites
steps.body: About two-thirds of production is white. Pinot Grigio, Chardonnay, Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Müller-Thurgau and Gewürztraminer are common. Gewürztraminer takes its name from Tramin, or Termeno, a village in Alto Adige. Alto Adige's whites are crisp, aromatic and precise.

steps.title: Native reds
steps.body: Lagrein gives deep, dark reds with plum, chocolate and firm tannins, and a rosé called Kretzer. Schiava, or Vernatsch, gives light, pale, fruity reds, like Santa Maddalena. Teroldego, in Trentino's Rotaliano plain, gives dark, juicy reds. Marzemino is another Trentino red. Pinot Noir, called Blauburgunder, is increasingly serious.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its character.
steps.explanation: The region grows many grapes in a small space.

steps.body: Schiava is one of the few red wines that's great lightly chilled. Its low tannin and fresh fruit suit summer.

steps.prompt: Gewürztraminer takes its name from which Alto Adige village?
steps.explanation: Tramin, or Termeno, is the grape's namesake.

steps.title: What you learned
points: About two-thirds of the region's wine is white
Lagrein, Schiava and Teroldego are native reds
Gewürztraminer is named after the village of Tramin
